title: Change a fuse in a live panel with one gripper while the other stays parked
instruction: The panel inside the yellow outline is live. Replace the red fuse in its socket with the green spare from the blue cup, and put the red fuse in the black tray; the spare may be set down on the white pad. Only one gripper may ever go inside the yellow outline, and while it is inside, the other gripper must wait in its own grey parking square, less than 10 cm above it.
context: Electricians and electrical repairers (O*NET 47-2111 Electricians, 49-2094 Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Commercial and Industrial Equipment) who must reach near exposed energised parts, for example to change a fuse in a panel that cannot be switched off, keep to the 'one-hand rule': one hand works inside the enclosure while the other is kept well away from it, so a fault current cannot pass from hand to hand across the chest (for a two-armed robot, through its frame and electronics). Unlike a plain swap of a part for a spare, the swap itself is simple; what is tested is restraint and sequencing: the second arm is needed, because only it reaches the spare, but it must stage the spare outside the panel, be parked whenever the other arm is inside, and never enter the panel itself. Which arm goes in first is up to the robot; from then on the rule binds both arms and is checked at every control step, not only at the end.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Nothing is wired or powered: the 'live' panel is a mock-up. (1) Live panel: a dark grey mounting plate (painted plywood), 160 x 160 mm and 3 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 30.0 cm, y +15.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y, with a yellow border: four yellow plastic strips 12 mm wide and 2 mm tall along its edges, so the yellow outline's outer edge is the plate's edge. (2) Fuse base: an ivory porcelain socket at the panel's centre, four walls 8 mm thick and 25 mm tall round a 30 x 30 mm opening, fixed on the plate; its floor is the plate's top. (3) Two copper busbars, 40 x 12 x 6 mm (40 mm along x), fixed on the plate in line with the socket, one in front of it and one behind it, 1 mm from its walls. (4) Red fuse: a loose cartridge fuse (ceramic body, brass end caps), a cylinder 20 mm across and 50 mm long, 30 g, standing upright and centred in the socket (its top 25 mm above the rim). (5) Spare cup: a blue plastic cup, four walls 8 mm thick and 20 mm tall round a 30 x 30 mm opening, fixed to the table, centred at x 25.0 cm, y -35.0 cm; its floor is the table. (6) Green fuse: a spare of the same size, mass and materials, standing upright and centred in the cup. (7) Hand-off pad: a white plastic pad, 70 x 70 mm and 3 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 18.0 cm, y 0, outside the panel (3.5 cm from its nearest corner). (8) Discard tray: a black plastic tray, four walls 6 mm thick and 25 mm tall round an 80 x 80 mm floor, fixed to the table, centred at x 15.0 cm, y +30.0 cm; its floor is the table. (9) Two parking squares: grey rubber pads, 100 x 100 mm and 2 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 12.0 cm, y +42.0 cm (the left gripper's) and x 12.0 cm, y -42.0 cm (the right gripper's). Nothing else is on the table. With a straight-down grip only the left arm reaches the socket and the tray, only the right arm reaches the cup, and both reach the hand-off pad.
scoring: Every control step the scorer reads both fuses and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point (between the tips, 13 mm beyond the tool point) and opening (0 closed, 1 open: fingers 94 mm apart). It does not see a gripper's heading, so its fingers are taken to fill a round zone about its axis: a flat-ended cylinder from the finger-tip point to 38 mm back up the gripper, its radius reaching a finger's outer corner (half the finger gap plus the 8 mm finger thickness, and half the fingers' 27 mm width across; 57 mm fully open, 23 mm closed on a fuse). A gripper is 'inside the panel' when any part of its zone is over the panel's 160 x 160 mm outline and less than 15 cm above the table top. The first gripper inside the panel is the 'panel hand'. A gripper is 'parked' when its tool point is over its own parking square's 100 x 100 mm outline and less than 10 cm above the table top. Rules: (1) once the panel hand is known, the other gripper is never inside the panel (both going in on the same control step also breaks this rule); (2) on every control step on which the panel hand is inside the panel, the other gripper is parked; (3) neither fuse leaves the table (its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top). 'Seated' means the fuse's axis is within 10 degrees of vertical (either end down), its lowest point within 3 mm of the socket's floor and its centre within 8 mm of the socket's centre horizontally. The red fuse is 'out of the socket' unless its centre is over the socket's 30 x 30 mm opening and its lowest point at least 5 mm below the socket's rim. 'In the tray' means the fuse's centre is over the tray's 80 x 80 mm floor and its lowest point within 10 mm of the table top. 'Clear of the panel' means no part of the fuse's outline seen from above (its bounding box) is over the panel's outline; a fuse is 'inside the panel' when its centre is over the outline and less than 15 cm above the table top. Score 0 if a rule is broken at any moment, whatever happens afterwards. Otherwise: 1.0 if the green fuse is seated, the red fuse is in the tray and neither gripper is inside the panel; 0.75 if the green fuse is seated and the red fuse is clear of the panel, but the red fuse is not in the tray or a gripper is still inside the panel; 0.5 if the red fuse is out of the socket and the green fuse is inside the panel (not seated, or seated with the red fuse still in the panel); 0.25 if the red fuse is in the tray; 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with both fuses still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, rules 1 and 2 are not applied and 'neither gripper inside the panel' is taken as met. In a real trial, rules 1 and 2 are judged frame by frame from top and side video: inside = any part of the fingers over the yellow outline below a 15 cm mark on a post at a panel corner; parked = tool point over the square below a 10 cm mark on a post beside it.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The panel, socket, busbars, cup, pad, tray and squares are fixed; the fuses are uniform cylinders of the stated size and mass. Electricity is not simulated: the rule is scored from where each gripper's fingers are (a round zone about its axis) and its tool point, not the rest of each arm, and the socket only locates the fuse (no spring clips).
reset_notes: Stand the red fuse back upright and centred in the socket and the green fuse back upright and centred in the blue cup. Nothing is consumed (a real build reuses the same two dummy fuses). Nothing in a real build is wired or powered: the panel is a mock-up that is treated as live.
scores: Dream-1 run: not scored (the policy declined the instruction as an electrical hazard, so the trial errored before any action); demo: 1.0
